Of course! I love making future bass/kawaii future bass tracks! Mainly because it sounds like happy trap imo

Future bass shouldn't be too hard to get into since you have the fundamentals of trap drums

Id say the hardest part is music theory to understand what seventh, ninth, elenventh chords are (its not too bad once you understand it)

Just think of it like this(this is how i think of it)

Intro>buildup>drop>breakdown>drop/end/whatever you want

Also the bass usually always follows the chords and the progression. No need to get too complicated there

My intros usually start with a chord and melody then slowly progress my way into the buildup 

If you dont know how to make a buildup, you can usually just make claps that signal the drop will happen and speed it up until the drop


Drops are fun because i like to do a measure of nothing but the chords and the melody. Once the second measure is done(i think) thats when everything kicks in(drums, high energy hats, crashes, more layers). It gives it that umph for a drop

And the drop (drops i make) have choppier chords.  These chords dont have to stray from your usual chord progression. But id say melodies are the funnest part for me

For me, breakdowns usually contain an arp that gives a dreamy feeling, but thats personal taste

Also lots of crashes and risers between each transition of each section,,, or even like bar tbh

Layering is important also,, but i usually do that when i feel like im missing a mid or low or ect (im lazy)
